quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, what does it mean?

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center of the road, you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Traffic is merging ahead.
A lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.
Use only the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot. Check several times before changing lanes. Keep watching both the traffic ahead and the traffic beside you.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about the bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Bad weather makes it hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to see. If you need windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic or pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the light changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic or pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic or pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending and you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the merging lane to speed up and match the traffic already on the interstate. Then merge smoothly when it is safe.

questions.question: You have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to the pedestrians.
You have the right of way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: When do large trucks lose speed?

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving through long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: A vehicle is coming toward you with its high beams on. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red. Is there any exception?

options.text: No exceptions.
Yes, if you entered on a yellow light.
Yes, if you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No exceptions.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a full stop. Check for traffic in all directions before you proceed.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow traffic light. If you have not already entered the intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: When a steady yellow light appears, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spot by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
Using your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors alone cannot show your blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check the area next to you.

questions.question: When backing up:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Mirrors do not show directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.
Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: When entering a work zone, slow down and be prepared to stop. Obey posted speed limits and watch for workers nearby.

questions.question: If a motorist sees pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should the motorist do?

options.text: Continue ahead. The motorist has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you of workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver moves faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster or slower than traffic flow increases collision risk.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking placards.

questions.question: Which of these statements is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure the next lane is clear.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian may be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these statements is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.
Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous and affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. Know how your medications affect your ability to drive.
